cues.say: Component 9: Holds that expire. Reserve the item first, then take payment. Unpaid holds expire. The status only moves forward: held, then paid or expired. You'll bring this up during version one and the spike, to protect what must never break.
Think of it as: A store setting an item aside for 10 minutes while you get your wallet. Use it for anything reserved before payment.
Here's a real scenario. A customer picks 2 pizzas for the 6:00 slot and clicks checkout.
Without it: Charge first, then find the slot is full.
With it: Reserve 2 of the slot's 150: held, expires in 10 minutes.
Pays on Stripe: webhook flips it to paid, kitchen gets it.
No payment in 10 minutes: sweeper releases the 2.
Why it works: You only take money for pizza you can actually make.
In the interview, say: Hold, then charge, so we never take money for something we can't deliver.
A few related terms you may hear.
State machine: The fixed statuses and allowed moves between them.
Forward only: A late Stripe message can't turn paid back into held.
